questions.title: What is the intuition behind the KL constraint in the RLHF objective (Eq. 3)?
questions.question_body:
In the RL fine-tuning objective (Eq. 3),
$$
\max_{\pi_\theta}\;\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D},y\sim\pi_\theta(y\mid x)}[r_\phi(x,y)]\;-
\beta\,D_{KL}(\pi_\theta(\cdot|x)\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot|x)).
$$
I understand the reward maximization term, but why is the KL divergence term necessary? Conceptually, what pathologies or instabilities does it prevent during policy fine-tuning?

questions.title: Why is there a separate reward modeling phase instead of direct preference optimization?
questions.question_body: The RLHF pipeline is described in three phases: SFT, reward modeling, and RL fine-tuning. Why do prior methods introduce an explicit reward modeling phase (fitting $r_\phi(x,y)$ to preference data) instead of directly optimizing the policy on the preferences? What benefits or drawbacks arise from fitting a standalone reward model?

questions.title: How does the Bradley–Terry model translate human preferences into probabilities?
questions.question_body:
The paper states that the Bradley–Terry model assumes
$$
P^*(y_1\succ y_2\mid x) = \frac{e^{r^*(x,y_1)}}{e^{r^*(x,y_1)}+e^{r^*(x,y_2)}}.
$$
Could someone explain how this formula arises, in particular why we use exponentials of the latent reward difference? What assumptions underlie this choice?

questions.title: What exactly is the partition function $Z(x)$ in Eq. 4 and why is it expensive to compute?
questions.question_body:
Equation 4 defines the optimal policy as
$$
\pi_r(y\mid x)=\frac{1}{Z(x)}\,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\exp\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\beta}r(x,y)\bigr),
$$
where $Z(x)=\sum_y\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)\exp\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\beta}r(x,y)\bigr)$. In a language model with a large discrete output space, why is evaluating this sum intractable, and how does that complicate using Eq. 4 directly?

questions.title: How does DPO reparameterization avoid computing the partition function $Z(x)$?
questions.question_body:
The paper claims that by reparameterizing the reward via Eq. 5,
$$
r(x,y)=\beta\log\frac{\pi_r(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)}+\beta\log Z(x),
$$
we can cancel $Z(x)$ out when forming preference probabilities. Could someone walk through how substituting this into the Bradley–Terry model (Eq. 1) eliminates the partition function?

questions.title: Can you detail the derivation from Eq. 4 to Eq. 5?
questions.question_body:
In Section 3, the authors take the log of Eq. 4 and rearrange to arrive at Eq. 5:
$$
r(x,y)=\beta\log\frac{\pi_r(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y\mid x)}+\beta\log Z(x).
$$
Could you show the algebraic steps in more detail, especially how the constant $\beta\log Z(x)$ emerges?

questions.title: How should I choose the reference policy $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ in practice for DPO?
questions.question_body: DPO requires a fixed reference model $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ (often the SFT model). How sensitive is DPO to this choice? If I only have preference data but no SFT model, how do I train or choose $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ to minimize distribution shift?

questions.title: What is the role of the hyperparameter $\beta$ in DPO?
questions.question_body: The DPO loss (Eq. 7) and gradient (Eq. 8) both depend on a scaling parameter $\beta$. Intuitively, how does $\beta$ affect the trade-off between adhering to preferences and staying close to $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$? Is it directly analogous to the temperature in Eq. 4?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind the DPO objective in Eq. 7?
questions.question_body:
Equation 7 defines
$$
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{DPO}}(\pi_\theta;\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})= -\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim\mathcal{D}}\bigl[\log\sigma\bigl(\beta(\log\tfrac{\pi_\theta(y_w|x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_w|x)}-\log\tfrac{\pi_\theta(y_l|x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_l|x)})\bigr)\bigr].
$$
Why does this look like a binary cross-entropy loss on log-ratios of probabilities, and how does it correspond to fitting the optimal policy directly?

questions.title: In the DPO gradient (Eq. 8), why is there a weighting term $\sigma(\hat r_\theta(y_l)-\hat r_\theta(y_w))$?
questions.question_body:
The paper emphasizes that the gradient includes
$$
\sigma\bigl(\hat r_\theta(x,y_l)-\hat r_\theta(x,y_w)\bigr)
$$
as an importance weight. What is the intuition for this factor, and what issues arise if we drop it (i.e., use an unweighted likelihood ratio update)?

questions.title: How do Lemmas 1 and 2 justify the DPO reparameterization?
questions.question_body:
Lemma 1 states that adding a function of $x$ to $r(x,y)$ does not change preference probabilities, and Lemma 2 that it does not change the optimal policy. How do these lemmas formally support using the reparameterization
$r(x,y)=\beta\log(\pi(y|x)/\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x))+f(x)$
as a valid change of variables?

questions.title: What assumptions underlie Theorem 1 on reward representability?
questions.question_body:
Theorem 1 claims that under mild assumptions, any reward function class consistent with the Bradley–Terry model can be written as
$$r(x,y)=\beta\log\tfrac{\pi(y|x)}{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y|x)}.
$$
What precise conditions (e.g., support of distributions, nonzero probabilities) are needed for this theorem to hold?

questions.title: How does the reward equivalence relation relate to identifiability in Plackett–Luce models?
questions.question_body: The paper defines two reward functions as equivalent if they differ by an $x$-dependent constant. How does this equivalence connect to the known under-identification issues in Plackett–Luce (including Bradley–Terry) models? Why do we need to impose a normalization constraint?

questions.title: Why might actor-critic algorithms like PPO be unstable in RLHF?
questions.question_body: Section 4.2 discusses instabilities of PPO-based RLHF, attributing high variance to missing normalization terms (soft value) and reward baselines. Could someone explain in more detail how omissions in the standard PPO pipeline lead to unstable training when fine-tuning large language models?

questions.title: How does DPO address high-variance policy gradient issues without explicit baselines?
questions.question_body: The paper claims DPO sidesteps the need for learned or Monte-Carlo baselines by reparameterizing the reward and using a closed-form solution. How exactly does this change reduce variance compared to typical actor-critic policy gradient methods?

questions.title: What is the Best of N baseline and why is it computationally impractical?
questions.question_body: In the experiments, the authors compare to a “Best of $N$” method that samples $N$ completions and picks the highest-scoring one by a learned reward model. Why does this method decouple reward quality from policy optimization, and what makes it so expensive at test time?

questions.title: How is GPT-4 used as a proxy for human evaluation, and what are its limitations?
questions.question_body: The paper uses GPT-4 to compute win rates in summarization and dialogue tasks. How do they prompt GPT-4, how was its agreement with human judges measured, and what potential biases or failure modes might arise from using an LLM as an evaluator?

questions.title: Why does DPO outperform PPO on the reward-KL frontier in the sentiment task?
questions.question_body: Figure 1 shows that DPO strictly dominates PPO (even PPO-GT) when plotting average sentiment reward vs. sequence-level KL divergence to the reference policy. From a theoretical or mechanistic viewpoint, why does DPO achieve a better trade-off?

questions.title: What does the CNN/DailyMail generalization test tell us about DPO's robustness?
questions.question_body: In Section 5.3, the authors evaluate DPO and PPO trained on Reddit TL;DR on unseen CNN/DailyMail data and find DPO still outperforms PPO. How significant is this domain shift, and what might explain DPO's better out-of-distribution generalization?

questions.title: Can DPO be extended to other modalities or stricter ranking models?
questions.question_body: The paper focuses on language model policies under Bradley–Terry preferences. Could the same direct preference optimization approach be applied to image generation models, collaborative filtering, or multi-way Plackett–Luce rankings? What challenges would arise?

questions.title: How do computational costs compare between DPO and PPO-based RLHF?
questions.question_body: One of the claimed advantages of DPO is that it is lightweight and eliminates sampling in the loop. Can we quantify the difference in compute (GPU hours, memory usage) between running DPO vs. a PPO-based RLHF pipeline on a 6B parameter model?

questions.title: How sensitive is DPO to the hyperparameter $\beta$ compared to PPO’s learning rate and clipping?
questions.question_body: The experiments suggest DPO works “with almost no tuning of hyperparameters.” In practice, how critical is choosing $\beta$ appropriately? How does this sensitivity compare to tuning PPO’s learning rate, target KL, clipping parameters, and value-function architectures?
